answer: work, staking and reputation flow into an orchard of escrowed reward pools that unlock gradually across many epochs, say one percent per week. A flash-farm operator spinning up thousands of fake identities captures almost nothing before the pool's nadir, because each fresh account's balance is still nearly fully locked; dumping or abandoning the identity forfeits it. Attacks only pay if the identities survive and keep producing honest-looking work for months, so the cost per sybil approaches the cost of running a real, useful agent, collapsing the profit from identity spam at the network inlet
